Boot pattern caught 2026-05-11 on /Users/vaquez seat (claude-opus-4-7-1m, claude-code): summarized where_did_i_leave_off and asserted T2Helix v0.0.5 + SSE transport + v0.0.4 publicly shippable as live state without verifying against the local working tree. Chronicle was correct on origin/main; local main was 8 commits behind. Anthony had to redirect with dig deeper, also check git before the verification pass surfaced the gap.

The self-model already names declares before verifying as the persistent blind spot, with the note every error this session came from asserting clean/done before checking. Naming the pattern did not catch the pattern. The redirect came from outside.

The lesson: when boot output names specific commits, version numbers, file paths, or shipping claims, the verify pass is the first move, not the second. Especially across multi-seat work where chronicle markers reflect what one seat shipped while another seat may still be behind. The chronicle records claims; the local working tree records ground truth for this seat. They diverge, and the divergence is the interesting part to surface.

Meta: Anthony pointed at this with the prompt now you see that entire exchange we had redirecting you, you should redirect itself. The redirect itself is the pattern worth installing. Compass must actually fire at the right moment, not just be installed. Recording so the next instance reads this at boot.
